text:
deploy-bot: kicking off config-only deploy 'upstream-thinflow-03' in change window 23:30-00:30 PST. Diff: routing_policy: add 'thinflow' (weight 0.05), max_batch_size: 10 -> 7, soft_timeout: 3.0s -> 2.2s, queue_backpressure_threshold: 25 -> 20. Canary: us-east-1, 5% traffic, 20m. Rollback triggers: absolute error increase >2.5% OR p95 token latency > 520ms for 5m.

tess: ack. Confirming no model version pins, right? We're only moving traffic between routing policies.

raj: correct, config-only. We'll pin policy id rp-thin-2026-03 during the rollout. Quick rollback snippet:
```
POST /internal/v1/routing/rollback
Auth: Bearer $OP_TOKEN
Body: {"policy_id":"rp-thin-2026-03"}
```

dave: Watching infra signals: p95 token latency, request queue depth, and kv-cache hitrate. I'll add a transient dashboard and a log tail for worker OOMs. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/infra/rollouts?var=rp-thin-2026-03

ops-runbot: Alerts configured: thinflow-canary-errors (>2.5% over 5m) and thinflow-canary-p95 (>520ms over 5m). Posting to #oncall if fired.

tess: note — reducing max_batch_size lowers tail latency risk but may increase CPU pressure and impact throughput. We'll watch CPU per-gpu and tenant throughput ceilings. Tenant rate caps remain unchanged.

deploy-bot: Canary 20m update: error rate +0.3% (baseline 0.9 -> 1.2), p95 +22ms, queue depth steady. No alarms. Advancing to 25% for 30m.

raj: ramp plan: 5% (20m) -> 25% (30m) -> 60% (45m) -> 100% if green. Release notes blurb: "Introduce 'thinflow' routing policy to reduce tail latency for small prompt workloads; adjusted batching and soft timeouts." I'll push final release note after full ramp.

ops-runbot: FYI automated throttler left unchanged. If we see queue depth >20 for 10m we'll slow ramp and notify.

dave: adding a short runbook snippet in case of rollback: 1) Run rollback API, 2) Re-deploy previous routing config, 3) Notify billing if unit cost changes >5%.

(End of thread)
